newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money rates steady, gilt volumes slip.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money rates steady, gilt volumes slip.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed at 8.25-8.75 percent on Wednesday, unchanged from the day's opening of 8.0-9.0 percent, dealers said.
"There was heavy demand for money in the market at the closing session from foreign banks, which took the call rates to 10 percent, before closing at 8.5 percent," a dealer at a state-run bank said.
He said the market reported some stray deals at 10 percent levels. A strike by Indian postal and telecommunications workers also disrupted operations briefly.
"There was slight panic in the market, they are not getting their positions due to lack of communication with branch and head offices," said Vinod Dixit, a forex dealer with Centurion Bank.
"Volumes on securities fell to 1.53 billion rupees on Wednesday against the Tuesday's volumes of 2.70 billion rupees," said Hitakshi Mehta at Apple Financial Securities Ltd.

Mehta said the 13.50 percent 1997 stock was traded at 12.20 percent against Tuesday's yield of 12.18 percent and 13.50 percent 1998 stock was traded at 12.96 unchanged from Tuesday's yield. The prices of 13.65 percent 1999 stock moved up from 100.70 rupees to 100.95 rupees, Mehta said.
The zero coupon bonds were traded at 13.59 percent and 13.78 percent for the 1999 and 2000 maturity bonds, unchanged from Tuesday's yield, Mehta said.
Treasury bills maturing in October 1997 were traded at 12.30 percent while January 1997 dealt at 8.95 percent, Mehta added.
Intercorporate deposits for P1+ rated companies were quoted at 19-20 percent while the P1-rated companies were in the region of 22-27 percent for 90 days, a dealer said.
The commercial paper was quoted in the region of 13.25-14.25 percent for P1+ rated companies while 90-days' maturity certificate of deposits were in the region of 12.50-14.0 percent, dealers said.
